title: Zigzag image-text layouts and decorative image fixations
statement:
In an eyetracking study of four real pages with about 30-35 participants per variation, informational images were studied in both zigzag (alternating) and aligned image-text layouts, but decorative images in zigzag rows caused stumbling fixations, so alternate image placement only for meaningful imagery or short sequences and align decorative images down one side.

Options:
- Aligned layout: Aligned two-column rows with all images on one side, for decorative or brand imagery (fits: clean, professional, calm)
- Zigzag with informational images: Zigzag rows only when every image carries real product information (product photos, digestible screenshots) (fits: visual, playful, storytelling)
- Short zigzag: Zigzag limited to two or three rows, where the short sequence keeps scanning easy (fits: modern, friendly, bold)
- Top-aligned decorative images: Decorative images top-aligned with their corresponding text so the eye is not pulled ahead of the copy (fits: polished, clean, clear)
- Left-first information: High-information content placed on the left side of the first row, where people start looking (fits: clear, practical, professional)
appliesWhen: Applies to: consumer apps, consumer subscriptions. Audience: general.

source.title: Zigzag Image–Text Layouts Make Scanning Less Efficient
